questions.question: The frequency of a sonometer wire is 100 Hz. If the length of the string is doubled and the tension is changed, the new frequency becomes 75 Hz. The ratio of the original and final tensions is

explanations.a: Incorrect. Check the frequency-tension relation f ∝ √T.
explanations.c: Correct. Based on f ∝ √T and L doubled, the correct tension ratio is 9:4.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Try squaring both sides of f ratio equation.

questions.question: A knife edge divides a sonometer wire in two parts which differ in lengths by 2 mm. The whole length of the wire is 1 metre. The two parts of the string when sounded together produce one beat per second. Then the frequencies of the smaller and longer parts are

explanations.a: Correct. A 1 cm length difference gives 1 Hz beat frequency.
explanations.b: Same values reversed. Order matters for the smaller part.
explanations.c: Incorrect frequency range. Try recalculating with beat frequency.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Not consistent with 1 m total length.

questions.question: A wire under tension vibrates with a frequency of 450 per second. What would be the fundamental frequency if the wire were half as long, twice as thick and under one-fourth tension?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Recalculate using frequency formula considering radius and tension.
explanations.b: Close, but not exact. Review √T and μ ∝ r² effect.
explanations.c: Correct. Accounts for all changes in string length, radius, and tension.
explanations.d: Not the right value. Double-check units and square root factors.

questions.question: The equation of transverse wave in a string is: y = 8 sin [1.256x - 25.12t] cm. What is the amplitude of the wave?

explanations.c: Correct. Amplitude is the coefficient before sine.

questions.question: Thermo emf of thermocouple depends on

explanations.a: Correct. Seebeck effect governs thermo emf generation.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Peltier relates to heat at junctions, not emf.
explanations.c: Related but not the primary cause of thermo emf.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Joule effect relates to heat due to current.
